segments.t: While Fedya teases Senya with a piece of ice for his fake toothache, Kostya tells Max that Nagiyev is a serious rival for Vika's heart. Listen to the full conversation in Russian first, and then we will walk through every line together.
Да я тебе говорю, надо полоскать.
Да, соперник у тебя, конечно, серьёзный.
Хорошо, что ему Настя не нравится.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Да я тебе говорю, надо полоскать.
'I am telling you, you need to rinse.' Fedya picks an honest style without hesitation, leaning on "govoryu" ("am telling") before closing the thought with "nado" ("it is necessary").
'Your medicine will not help at all.' Fedya offers a steady rhythm on the spot, joining "lekarstvo" ("medicine") to "sovsem" ("at all") so every word pulls its weight.
'Right here is real cold ice.' Fedya establishes a wry stance for Kostya, putting "nastoyashchiy" ("real, genuine") alongside "kholodnyy" ("cold") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Here, you can check for yourself.' Fedya sets a playful approach in front of Max, putting "mozhesh" ("can") alongside "proverit" ("to check, verify") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Well, have you checked already?' Fedya challenges bluntly in their exchange, joining "uzhe" ("already, now") to "proveril" ("checked") so every word pulls its weight.
Да, соперник у тебя, конечно, серьёзный.
'Yes, your rival is certainly serious.' Kostya shares a steady tack in their talk, combining "u tebya" (literally "by you") with "sopernik" ("rival") rather than a separate word for "have".
Хорошо, что ему Настя не нравится.

'It is good that he does not like Nastya.' Kostya establishes a serious manner in this beat, putting "khorosho" ("good, fine") alongside "nravitsya" ("is pleasing") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'I will go talk with him calmly.' Max chooses a candid angle as they talk, putting "poydu" ("go") alongside "spokoyno" ("calmly") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Max, wait, where are you going?' Kostya tests candidly with Fedya now, putting "podozhdi" ("wait") alongside "kuda" ("where to") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Dmitry Vladimirovich, are you free right now?' Max inquires sharply as the talk turns, combining "seychas" ("now") and "svobodny" ("free") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Let me call you back later.' Kostya chooses a natural line on the spot, pairing "day" ("give") with "pozzhe" ("later") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'We need to talk seriously.' Max shares a warm view in this beat, joining "nuzhno" ("necessary") to "seryozno" ("seriously") so every word pulls its weight.
Да я тебе говорю, надо полоскать.
Да, соперник у тебя, конечно, серьёзный.
Хорошо, что ему Настя не нравится.
Max marches straight up to Nagiyev's table to settle things man to man, only to learn something unexpected. Until next time!
